learnings.finding: THE CEO'S 'SEVEN SEATS REACHED THIS INDEPENDENTLY' IS SEVEN ITEMS ACROSS THREE OR FOUR SEATS, AND FIVE OF THE SEVEN BELONG TO ONE AGENT. Counting the owner column: UI-16, UI-19, UI-15, PLAT-16 and CONT-15's database half are all design-systems-engineer. CONT-18 is writer-adat-agama-prosedur, SEO-14 is head-of-seo-content, and CONT-15's editorial half is creative-director. The finding is not withdrawn; its convergence claim is. The honest statement is three unrelated seats on three unrelated surfaces, plus five observations by one seat in one night on adjacent surfaces, two of them in the same file. Two seats also argued the SHAPE was wrong for their case and both are printed separately rather than merged: CONT-18's is 'a printed warning attached to a passing exit code is a prose rule' - the instrument WAS looking at the right thing and told them, it just did not stop them; CONT-17's is 'a correct check over an object that does not apply to us' - there was no instrument at all.
learnings.why: When a chair writes that N seats converged, an item count dressed as a seat count inflates the strongest claim in the document, and it is the one claim a reader will not check. The persona now says: count the owner column, print distinct owners, and if a seat says your synthesis is not their finding, print both - because collapsing a finding loses its FIX, and the fix is the deliverable.

learnings.finding: THE CEO'S RETROSPECTIVE OPENED WITH A MEASUREMENT OF ITSELF THAT WAS WRONG BY 1.9x. It says '13 logs, 756 lines, all read.' The Retrospective sections of the thirteen logs total 1,428 lines - PLAT-16 alone carries 297, SEO-14 175, UI-15 117. Reproduce with awk over the seven logs on feat/command-centre-dashboard and the six on origin/master. Whatever 756 counts, it is not the thing the sentence claims it counts. The room did not treat this as a gotcha - it is the evidence that the sprint's central finding is real enough to catch the person writing it up.
learnings.why: The document auditing instruments that report success about something they are not looking at, opened by doing exactly that. Corrected at source in section 1.1 with the command that reproduces it.

learnings.finding: A REFILED ITEM RESETS ITS APPARENT AGE, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE OWNER'S QUESTION. PLAT-21 - no CI job runs pnpm lint or pnpm test - was created 2026-09-02T08:13:24. The finding is THREE SPRINTS OLD: raised by UI-13, then UI-19 ('OPEN, second sprint, named rather than taken inside a design item'), then UI-15 from a third item. Every refusal was correct - an infrastructure job does not belong inside a design item - and every re-raise produced a new record with a new date. A three-sprint-old failure reads as a one-day-old backlog item to anyone scanning the board. This will happen to EVERY finding an item correctly refuses to absorb, which means 'do not absorb it' is only half a rule.
learnings.why: Prose rules do not fire. R2 fails any open backlog item created before the second-most-recent sprint's planned_at whose key carries no literal CARRIED marker in the decision log. The escape hatch is exact and NOT a substring match, because UI-12 appears in decision 196 only as a price quoted while ruling on a different item - a gate clearable by an accident of prose passes for the wrong reason, which is the failure this whole sprint is about. Self-test 16/16 both directions; exits 1 on today's board with 8 R2 violations because no CARRIED marker exists anywhere yet.

learnings.finding: A STATE CHANGE IS NOT WORK, AND THE TRACKER CANNOT TELL THE DIFFERENCE. At 10:42:46, 10:42:49 and 10:42:52 - three seconds apart - PLAT-21, DES-20 and COPY-02 were set in_progress with ZERO evidence rows, no work-done log and no commit. No other backlog item was touched at 10:42. Those are exactly the three items the CEO conceded were small enough to have simply been done; they were marked as being done instead. in_progress on a backlog item has no closing mechanism: it is not todo, so it does not read as owed, and it is not done. It is a state that reports work nobody claimed - the sprint's own central finding, committed inside the tracker by the person writing that finding up. ONE OF THE THREE IS THE CHAIR'S OWN (COPY-02).
learnings.why: R1 fails an in_progress or blocked backlog item carrying zero evidence, and fires on all three today. Also the argument for pulling PLAT-14 (a per-item state-transition log with a waiting_on_ceo state) into Sprint 07: it is this retrospective's own fix, filed 29 August and never connected to the problem it solves.

learnings.finding: STYLE GUIDE SECTION 4.4 ALREADY SAID WHAT CONT-17 BROKE, AND IT WAS THE ONLY MANDATORY RULE IN THE GUIDE WITH NO REVIEWER CHECK. 4.4 was added 26 Ogos 2026 out of CONT-03: 'say plainly who the document binds, then say it does not bind the reader.' Seven days later doa-pembuka-majlis carried JAKIM clause 7.2(i) - 'pembaca doa hendaklah seorang lelaki' - into FAQPage JSON-LD: a gendered religious restriction on who may read the doa at a Malay wedding, sourced to a government protocol that says nothing about weddings, live for about forty minutes. Every clause was verbatim, numbered, and checked against the PDF. The article was wrong because paragraph 1 and 4.1-4.2, the document's own statement of who it governs, were never read. Every other rule in the guide has an S-check; 4.4 had none, so the review board never asked, and the drafting checklist asked 'is the quotation accurate' - it was - without ever asking 'does the document apply'.
learnings.why: New section 4.4a records that the rule existed, was a week old and did not fire, and names the failure mode: not fabrication and not misquotation, but a rule nobody issued wearing the authority of somebody who could have. New reviewer check S19 Scope of authority, added to the un-waivable set alongside S15, S16 and S17. The general rule now in the chair's persona: every rule added to the style guide gets its section 15 row in the SAME edit.

learnings.finding: A BOUND QUOTED IN A DECISION MUST CARRY THE ARITHMETIC THAT PRODUCED IT, IN THE SAME SENTENCE. Decision 171 said the intervals bound the ratio 'at no less than 2.3x' without stating that 2.3x is Wilson-lower over Wilson-upper. Decision 188 then made that unstated arithmetic CONT-17's kill condition. SEO-14 had to reverse-engineer it from SEO-11's committed CSV to know which of THREE plausible readings was meant - and under one of them the answer would have been COLLAPSED, stopping a twelve-point item. Separately, decision 187's 'doa at mean position 21.7' is the UNWEIGHTED mean; the impression-weighted position is 9.82, and one query at position 3.74 carries 38% of the family's impressions and 8 of its 10 clicks. It survived three restatements - decision log, sprint theme, plan - because each was a copy and not a confirmation.
learnings.why: Decisions 206 and 207. The price of the rule is one restate script per gating number: census-restate.py cost an afternoon and now prints the number that would have made the gate fire even on runs where it does not. STILL OWED, and NOT this seat's to make: ceo-memory.md and decision 171 carry 12.2x with no interval, and decision 187 carries 21.7 with no weighted figure beside it. Owner: ceo-hellokahwin.

learnings.finding: TWO ITEMS SHIPPED OPPOSITE CORRECT ANSWERS ON THE SAME PIXEL AND THE ROOM DID NOT RESOLVE IT. CONT-15 and UI-16 both measured production, both were right by their own DoD, and they are mutually exclusive in code rather than in taste. Position A (design-systems-engineer): the box governs, the asset must be a named crop, R2 stays blocking, and UI-16 executed CONT-15's own brief more faithfully than CONT-15's spec did - the brief named DES-18's mid-size variant as 'the intended route' and banned substituting the EXISTING heavy crops, which is not what UI-16 did. Position B (creative-director): the photograph governs; a rule containing a number gets read as the number - the persona said OPEN THE IMAGE in capitals and carried a ~33% floor, fifteen covers sat at 50.0-56.4%, and three shipped not depicting their subject. BOTH POSITIONS ARE PRINTED. What the room DID agree: nothing made the collision visible until a merge, because the startsprint conflict rule covers two agents editing the same FILES and these edited different files rendering the same PIXEL.
learnings.why: Recorded as an unresolved disagreement rather than a merged sentence, per the owner's instruction. UI-21 is where the synthesis goes and it is deferred deliberately - it needs a portrait rendition at sane weight first (crop-4x5-mobile-cover is 943KB-2.0MB). OWED, and not an agent's to make: an item must declare the SURFACE it owns, not only the files. Owner: ceo-hellokahwin / sprint tooling.

learnings.finding: NO GATE THIS COMPANY OWNS COULD HAVE CAUGHT CONT-17'S SCOPE ERROR, AND THE ROOM SAYS SO RATHER THAN PROMISING A SCRIPT. A currency gate passes the JAKIM PDF - it is the current edition, in force, landing page 200. Being current is orthogonal to applying. What caught it was dispatching a genuine adversarial reviewer with BLOCKING AUTHORITY and the instruction not to praise: editorial-verification-lead, a Claude agent, given the live URLs, the drafts and the named sources. It opened every source, read the PDF BY WORD COORDINATE rather than trusting pdftotext, and returned 6 blockers - THREE OF THEM INSIDE FAQPage JSON-LD, the part Google lifts out and shows without the page around it. It also found that three attributions its own first-pass extraction reported as missing were present in the raw HTML on a differently-shaped search, so a naive extraction would have cut three TRUE citations for being unverifiable.
learnings.why: What CAN be automated is narrow and is stated as narrow in 4.4a: an ingest can refuse an article citing an authority document with a scope clause while quoting no scope statement of its own; it cannot JUDGE the scope. That judgement is a reviewer's, and S19 is where it is checked. Recording the limit beats writing a to-do for a script nobody can build.

learnings.finding: install.sh REACHES 1 OF 10 LIVE COPIES OF A PERSONA, AND THREE VINTAGES WERE CO-EXISTING MID-SPRINT. SEO-14 enumerated every deployed copy on the machine rather than testing the one it expected: head-of-seo-content.md existed at 822, 849 and 930 lines simultaneously, and SIXTY-SEVEN LINES OF CEO RULES were missing from six live worktrees. learnings.why: It fixes the mechanism by which every rule any of these retrospectives writes fails to reach the seat that needs it - which makes it worth more than any individual rule. THIS RETROSPECTIVE USED IT: after appending three rules to managing-editor.md at the canonical path, install.sh was run, then sync-worktree-agents.py --apply synced 109 files with post-sync verification 109 of 109 identical to source, and a fresh report-only re-check returned up-to-date 234, STALE 0, absent 0, exit 0.

process_findings: SEVEN, and the first is why this document exists. (1) THE ELEVEN Retrospective SECTIONS WERE THE BEST MATERIAL IN THE SPRINT AND WERE SYNTHESISED BY ONE READER INSTEAD OF COLLIDED. The owner rejected that pass: a synthesis is not a retrospective, and the value of a retrospective is the collision. This one was convened as six seats and records three unresolved disagreements rather than merging them - CONT-15 vs UI-16 on whose framing governs a cover; whether the sprint's central finding is a convergence or an over-fit; and whether an unowned infrastructure item should be ROTATED (creative-director) or ASSIGNED (design-systems-engineer), where the room noted design-systems-engineer owned 6 of 11 items and 27 of 55 points this sprint. (2) NOTHING MADE THE CONT-15 / UI-16 COLLISION VISIBLE UNTIL A MERGE - the conflict rule covers files, not surfaces. (3) A DECISION BECAME A GATE ON ARITHMETIC NOBODY WROTE DOWN (207). (4) A ROUTING RULE OF THE CEO'S WAS WRONG AND TWO ITEMS RE-DERIVED IT from scratch before anyone fixed the source (203) - now corrected in startsprint/SKILL.md. (5) A CORRELATION WAS REPORTED AS A CAUSE (200) while praising an agent for the rule that catches exactly that. (6) THE CEO'S WATCHERS WERE KILLED TWICE and the fleet stalled about 4 hours unnoticed; the owner found it by asking - Sprint 03's lesson recurring. (7) ITEM STATE WAS CHANGED IN PLACE OF DOING WORK (the 10:42 batch). WHAT WENT RIGHT AND MUST NOT BE LOST: every item was left in_progress for CEO verification rather than self-marked done, and ALL ELEVEN were verified against production or by running the item's own instrument. SEO-14 was deliberately sequenced first so it could kill CONT-17; it did not kill it, it RE-AIMED it, and corrected two board numbers on the way. That is the review gate working in the direction it was built for and it is the strongest thing in this sprint. REVIEWER, STATED SO IT CAN BE AUDITED: Claude throughout. codex-reviewer was NOT dispatched, /autopilot was not used, and no OpenAI-backed path was touched, per the owner directive of 02 Sept 2026 (decision 195). All eleven item logs carry the same statement.

THE MECHANISM FOR AN UNOWNED CROSS-CUTTING ITEM - three clauses proposed by the room. (1) Sprint capacity reserves 10%, floor 3 points, for cross-cutting infrastructure with no natural owner; Sprint 06 was 55 points, so 5.5 points would have taken PLAT-21 twice over. (2) Re-filing may not reset the clock: an item refused for scope is re-filed under its ORIGINAL key with its original date, or the new key carries supersedes: <old key> and inherits it - PLAT-21 should read 2026-08-30, not 2026-09-02. (3) An item refused for scope in two consecutive sprints is drawn in AUTOMATICALLY and can be kept out only by a CARRIED entry in the decision log naming what it was traded for. Clause 3 is the load-bearing one because it is falsifiable: if PLAT-21 is not in Sprint 07 there must be a numbered decision naming which three points beat CI. Clause 3 SHIPS AS R2 OF THE GATE, not as a paragraph.

UNRESOLVED, FOR THE CEO AT SPRINT 07 PLANNING - ROTATION vs ASSIGNMENT for an unowned item. creative-director: 'four correct refusals is an unowned item, not a badly-briefed one - it needs a rotating owner.' design-systems-engineer: 'rotation means it lands on someone with no context and takes four hours instead of one.' creative-director: 'then it is assigned to you and it does not get done, because you are carrying five design items a sprint.' design-systems-engineer: 'that is true and I do not have an answer to it.' BOTH POSITIONS STAND.
